chunks: From him, from al-Nadr, from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah al-Madaini, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When you are invited to the testimony (of faith), then respond.

key_terms.الشَّهَادَةِ: The testimony of faith (Shahadah), specifically the declaration that there is no god but Allah and Muhammad is His messenger.
key_terms.فَأَجِبْ: Then respond/answer (imperative), indicating a recommended or obligatory promptness in accepting the call.

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on responding to an invitation to declare the Shahadah?
ai.summary: In the context of *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the communal obligation of *Shahadah* as a public declaration of truth, particularly during times of trial or when testifying in legal matters. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that accepting the call to bear witness is not merely a personal affirmation but a duty to uphold divine truth in society, linking individual faith with public testimony.
